lever: Iron-rich foods, especially meat and fish
intervention: Eating iron-rich foods, especially meat and fish (haem iron)
summary: Iron from meat and fish (haem iron) is absorbed much better than iron from plants, and meat also helps absorb plant iron eaten in the same meal. Lentils, beans, tofu and seeds still provide useful iron, especially with vitamin C.
whyThisGrade: Consistent absorption studies, summarised in reviews
How much is absorbed depends on your iron stores and the rest of the meal
caution: Iron is absorbed less well from plant foods than the numbers suggest. Spinach, for example, is left out because it also contains substances that block iron absorption.
